answer: Operator-Linked Resource Ledger. Each new identity must draw from an operator's shared allocation of a scarce public good—say, verified compute cycles or metered network timber—and every allocation is logged against the operator's real-world account, not the wallet. When one operator's identities exceed a threshold, the ledger throttles all of them, severing the bridge between sock puppets and their sponsor. A gale of duplicated signups then costs the operator its entire future capacity, not a disposable key.
